title: Tech Note: XML Structure Import/Export in 4D v11 SQL
author: Atanas Atanassov, Technical Services Team Member, 4D Inc.

historical_commentary.text: This note documents the groundbreaking Structure Export/Import feature introduced in 4D v11 SQL Release 1 (2007), enabling database structures to be serialized as XML files and reconstructed programmatically—a capability that predated 4D's later REST/ORDA era and enabled template-based database provisioning and structure cloning. It provides a thorough XML primer (syntax, DOM vs. SAX parsing models, XPath notation) grounded in Apache's Xerces and Xalan libraries underpinning 4D's XML support. While XML remains ubiquitous, the specific XML-based structure import/export feature was superseded by REST APIs and ORDA (2018+), and most modern development avoids XML in favor of JSON; the note is now primarily of historical interest to legacy 4D database maintainers.
related_updates: 4D v12+ (2012) introduced REST APIs as the modern interoperability standard
ORDA (2018+) became the preferred data access layer, with native JSON serialization
XML-based structure cloning was never widely adopted; developers typically used 4D's GUI structure editor instead
JSON has become the de facto standard for data serialization in web/REST contexts, replacing XML in most use cases
